## Verdict
needs-revision

## Concerns
- `claim-1` is not established by the supplied record. The accepted child certificate covers only \(i,j\ge3\); no coordinate matrices are displayed for the \(i=2\) or \(j=2\) deletion cases.
- The report asserts, but does not prove, that \(r_1,\ldots,r_8\) generate the complete degree-\(d+3\) row lattice. The stated graded decomposition and reductions require a checkable derivation.
- The required independently derived \(R_{\mathrm{full}}\), coefficient matrices \(\mathcal C\), products \(\mathcal C R_{\mathrm{selected}}\), and unit determinants are absent for the fifteen new threshold cases.

## Unresolved certificates
- [proof-attempt] Supply the fifteen tables indexed by \((i,j)\in\{(2,2),(2,3),(3,2)\}\) and \((p,c)\in\{(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1),(3,1)\}\), explicitly deleting every unavailable \(A,\ldots,J\) slot. For each table, independently enumerate \(R_{\mathrm{full}}\), display \(R_{\mathrm{selected}}\) and \(\mathcal C\), verify \(\mathcal C R_{\mathrm{selected}}=R_{\mathrm{full}}\) entrywise, give the relevant unit determinant, and prove that the eight Pieri products generate the entire degree-\(d+3\) row lattice.
